chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Bat'tat said: Narrated to us Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saf'far, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboob, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abdul-Aziz, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa al-Jahani, on the authority of Hurayz ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The people regarding fate are in three states: A man who claims that God, the Exalted, forced people to commit sins, this one has wronged God in His decree, so he is a disbeliever. And a man who claims that the matter has been delegated to them, this one has weakened God in His dominion, so he is a disbeliever. And a man who says: Indeed God, the Exalted, burdened the servants with what they can bear and did not burden them with what they cannot bear. So when he does good, he praises God, and when he does bad, he seeks God's forgiveness. This one is a true Muslim, and God is the Grantor of Success.
ai.seo_question: What are the three classifications of people regarding divine decree (Qadar) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a definitive exposition of the Shia doctrine of 'al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn' (the position between compulsion and full delegation), rejecting the extremes of Jabriyyah and Qadariyyah. By affirming that God commands only what is within human capacity, the text establishes a balanced theological framework where human agency operates within divine sovereignty, necessitating gratitude for success and repentance for failure.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-272 Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami and Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Bat’tat quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saf’far, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboob, and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Abdul-Aziz, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa al-Jahani, on the authority of Hurayz ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

The people can be classified into three groups regarding the issue of fate. There are those who think that the Exalted the Honorable God has forced the people to commit sins. Such people have wronged the Exalted the Honorable God with their decree. They are atheists. There are others who think that running all the affairs has been turned over to them. Such people have undermined God’s Kingdom. Thus, they are atheists. There are also those who say, ‘The Honorable the Exalted God has placed such a burden upon His servants that they can bear. God has not overburdened the people to such an extent which they cannot stand. Once they do good, they praise God. And once they do bad, they seek God’s forgiveness.’ Such people are true Muslims. It is God who grants success.
